description: Mode-specific parity fixtures for process creation (posix_spawn, exec family). Strict: standard POSIX semantics. Hardened: launch surface validation + environment sanitization.

cases.name: posix_spawn_nonexistent_strict
cases.note: posix_spawn fails with ENOENT for nonexistent binary

cases.name: execve_replaces_process_strict
cases.note: fl's execve and the host's each run in their own forked child on this same input; the token is a parity verdict on what the kernel did with that child. A child that RETURNS from execve exits 127, so a wrapper that fails to exec cannot pass. Previously the executor returned a hardcoded NO_RETURN and never called execve. bd-7t61h9

cases.name: execve_eacces_strict
cases.note: execve is called for real, on this same input, against BOTH fl and the host; the token is a parity verdict, not a pinned errno. Previously the executor returned a hardcoded -1 because the pathname was /etc/passwd and never called execve. bd-7t61h9

cases.name: system_returns_status_strict
cases.note: system() runs command and returns exit status

cases.name: posix_spawn_echo_hardened
cases.note: Hardened: validates executable path and sanitizes environment before launch

cases.name: system_returns_status_hardened
cases.note: Hardened: same semantics, emits spawn evidence for audit chain
